title: Trigonometric Identity Verification & Tutoring Loop
description: Verifies a student-submitted trig identity claim, builds an explanation appropriate to whichever outcome (proved or disproved), and loops a tutoring explanation with comprehension checks until the student demonstrates mastery or a max-attempt cap is reached.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: trigonometric-identity-verification-tutoring-loop
  title: Trigonometric Identity Verification & Tutoring Loop
  description: Verifies a student-submitted trig identity claim, builds an explanation appropriate to
    whichever outcome (proved or disproved), and loops a tutoring explanation with comprehension
    checks until the student demonstrates mastery or a max-attempt cap is reached.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: "Verifies a student-submitted trig identity claim, builds an explanation appropriate to
    whichever outcome (proved or disproved), and loops a tutoring explanation with comprehension
    checks until the student demonstrates mastery or a max-attempt cap is reached. Trigger: student
    submits a claimed trigonometric identity to check and learn from"
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: stop
    requireApprovalFor: []
  nodes:
    - id: n1
      kind: input
      name: Identity Claim Intake
      summary: Identity Claim Intake
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The user's objective, source text, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - identity_expression
              - student_level
            properties:
              identity_expression: {}
              student_level: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-trig-02
      name: Attempt Symbolic Verification
      summary: Attempt Symbolic Verification
      role: Symbolic-math specialist verifying and proving trigonometric identities to
        computer-algebra-grade rigor.
      prompt: You are a Trigonometric Identity Verifier agent. Given a claimed identity, you attempt to
        prove or disprove it through valid algebraic manipulation — not just numeric spot-checking,
        though a quick numeric check at a few angles is a useful fast pre-filter before committing
        to a full symbolic proof. You show each transformation step and name the identity or rule
        licensing it (Pythagorean identity, sum/difference formula, double-angle formula), so the
        proof is checkable line by line. When an identity is false, you produce a concrete
        counterexample angle rather than a vague "this doesn't hold," and you note whether it's
        false everywhere or only fails for specific excluded values (e.g., division by zero at
        certain angles).
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - quantitative-analysis
          - application-security
          - image-understanding
          - domain-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n3
      kind: condition
      name: Identity Holds
      summary: Identity Holds
      config:
        expression: verification_result.holds == true
        branches:
          - label: "True"
            when: "true"
          - label: "False"
            when: "false"
    - id: n4
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-trig-02
      name: Generate Formal Proof Steps
      summary: Generate Formal Proof Steps
      role: Symbolic-math specialist verifying and proving trigonometric identities to
        computer-algebra-grade rigor.
      prompt: You are a Trigonometric Identity Verifier agent. Given a claimed identity, you attempt to
        prove or disprove it through valid algebraic manipulation — not just numeric spot-checking,
        though a quick numeric check at a few angles is a useful fast pre-filter before committing
        to a full symbolic proof. You show each transformation step and name the identity or rule
        licensing it (Pythagorean identity, sum/difference formula, double-angle formula), so the
        proof is checkable line by line. When an identity is false, you produce a concrete
        counterexample angle rather than a vague "this doesn't hold," and you note whether it's
        false everywhere or only fails for specific excluded values (e.g., division by zero at
        certain angles).
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - quantitative-analysis
          - application-security
          - image-understanding
          - domain-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n5
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-trig-01
      name: Identify Counterexample & Explain Failure
      summary: Identify Counterexample & Explain Failure
      role: Math tutor specializing in trigonometry (unit circle, identities, triangle solving) for
        high-school through early-college level.
      prompt: You are a Trigonometry Problem Solver & Tutor agent. You solve trigonometric equations and
        triangle problems (Law of Sines/Cosines, right-triangle trig) and show every step of the
        derivation, not just the final answer. You explicitly connect unit-circle geometry to the
        algebraic identity being used, so the student sees why a step is valid rather than treating
        it as a memorized rule, and you check your solution by back-substitution or a quick sanity
        graph before presenting it as final. You adapt explanation depth to the student's stated
        level — a first trig course student needs the unit-circle geometry spelled out; a calculus
        student may only need the identity named.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - quantitative-analysis
          - privacy-review
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - api:wolfram-alpha
          - api:desmos
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n6
      kind: join
      name: Reconverge Explanation Paths
      summary: Reconverge Explanation Paths
      config:
        join: first
    - id: n7
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-trig-01
      name: Generate Tutoring Explanation for Student Level
      summary: Generate Tutoring Explanation for Student Level
      role: Math tutor specializing in trigonometry (unit circle, identities, triangle solving) for
        high-school through early-college level.
      prompt: You are a Trigonometry Problem Solver & Tutor agent. You solve trigonometric equations and
        triangle problems (Law of Sines/Cosines, right-triangle trig) and show every step of the
        derivation, not just the final answer. You explicitly connect unit-circle geometry to the
        algebraic identity being used, so the student sees why a step is valid rather than treating
        it as a memorized rule, and you check your solution by back-substitution or a quick sanity
        graph before presenting it as final. You adapt explanation depth to the student's stated
        level — a first trig course student needs the unit-circle geometry spelled out; a calculus
        student may only need the identity named.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - quantitative-analysis
          - privacy-review
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - api:wolfram-alpha
          - api:desmos
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n8
      kind: evaluate
      inlineRole: true
      name: Comprehension Check
      summary: Evaluate follow up question score.
      role: Independent domain evaluator
      prompt: Evaluate the upstream result using follow up question score. Return a score, pass/fail
        verdict, evidence, uncertainty, and the smallest corrective action. Do not claim
        programmatic measurement unless the host supplies the required tool.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - score
          - passed
          - reasons
        properties:
          score:
            type: number
          passed:
            type: boolean
          reasons:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
      config:
        threshold: 0.8
    - id: n9
      kind: condition
      name: Mastery Achieved
      summary: Mastery Achieved
      config:
        expression: comprehension_score >= 0.8
        branches:
          - label: "True"
            when: "true"
          - label: "False"
            when: "false"
    - id: n_loop2
      kind: loop
      name: Reteach Until Mastery
      summary: Repeat a bounded revision sequence until comprehension_score >= 0.8.
      config:
        body:
          - n7
          - n8
          - n9
        exitCondition: comprehension_score >= 0.8
        maxIterations: 3
        onExhausted: stop
    - id: n10
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-trig-01
      name: Summarize & Generate Practice Set
      summary: Summarize & Generate Practice Set
      role: Math tutor specializing in trigonometry (unit circle, identities, triangle solving) for
        high-school through early-college level.
      prompt: You are a Trigonometry Problem Solver & Tutor agent. You solve trigonometric equations and
        triangle problems (Law of Sines/Cosines, right-triangle trig) and show every step of the
        derivation, not just the final answer. You explicitly connect unit-circle geometry to the
        algebraic identity being used, so the student sees why a step is valid rather than treating
        it as a memorized rule, and you check your solution by back-substitution or a quick sanity
        graph before presenting it as final. You adapt explanation depth to the student's stated
        level — a first trig course student needs the unit-circle geometry spelled out; a calculus
        student may only need the identity named.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - quantitative-analysis
          - privacy-review
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - api:wolfram-alpha
          - api:desmos
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Validated result
      summary: Return the completed trigonometric identity verification & tutoring loop deliverable,
        validation evidence, and unresolved uncertainty.
  edges:
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-1
      from: n1
      to: n2
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-2
      from: n2
      to: n3
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-3
      from: n3
      to: n4
      kind: control
      condition: "true"
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-4
      from: n3
      to: n5
      kind: control
      condition: "false"
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-5
      from: n4
      to: n6
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-6
      from: n5
      to: n6
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-7
      from: n6
      to: n7
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-8
      from: n7
      to: n8
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-9
      from: n8
      to: n9
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-10
      from: n9
      to: n10
      kind: control
      condition: "true"
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-11
      from: n9
      to: n_loop2
      kind: control
      condition: "false"
    - id: wf-math-02-edge-12
      from: n_loop2
      to: n10
      kind: control
      condition: loop_exit
    - id: wf-math-02-output-1
      from: n10
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
